intent: Revert to the best-raced geometry (±0.03 m row, 16 mm, y = 0.04) and keep the Integrator's kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller, so this race is a clean read of the best layout. I changed the row back from ±0.04 m because iteration 8 already tested ±0.04 m at kp 1.2 and scored 61.35, which is worse than ±0.03 m. I kept everything else unchanged. Expected result: about 69.46, with max error near 0.062 m and line loss at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run. Next, I am considering a 12 mm footprint at the same ±0.03 m positions to test whether 16 mm edge noise is raising s-bend oscillation (0.168), but I am not committing to it yet, because its reach falls to about 0.0485 m and that may cost coverage at the edge.
learning: Iteration 8 settled the widening question: ±0.04 m at kp 1.2 gives 61.35, so the row widening is not a gain-only effect and the ±0.03 m row is preferred. Open hypotheses: (1) the 0.06 m off-track limit is fixed by body width and cannot be moved, so gains come only from keeping the robot on the line, through sensing or controller response; (2) 16 mm footprint edge noise adds s-bend oscillation, and a 12 mm footprint at ±0.03 m would reduce it at the cost of about 2 mm of edge reach; (3) line loss at 1.0 per run may occur at start-up or at entry rather than at the row edge. Please report the progress at the first line-loss event on each track and the max error at that moment, so the loss can be attributed to coverage or to controller overshoot.
rationale:
Evidence across iterations 0 to 8 points to one conclusion. The ±0.03 m row at 16 mm with y = 0.04 is the best-raced geometry (69.46 in iterations 3, 5, 6 and 7, identical each time, so the simulator is deterministic for this layout). Every race ends off track at max error about 0.062 m, against the 0.06 m limit. Body width cannot relax that limit inside its allowed range, since the limit only exceeds 0.06 m above 0.19 m width. Line loss stays at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run.

The ±0.04 m row has now been tested at kp 1.2 with kd 0.4, which is the isolating test the Integrator asked for. Iteration 8 scored 61.35, with progress 0.17 on the oval, 0.16 on the s-bend and 0.116 on the slalom, and its per-track metrics match iteration 4 almost exactly. So the widening is worse on its own, not only at kp 1.0. The gain change was not the sole cause. I therefore do not take the Integrator's request to hold ±0.04 m for another race, because that race would repeat a result already measured. The Integrator's feedback calls iteration 9 an isolating test, but iteration 8 already ran it.

I am reverting to the best-raced row: five sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.04, 16 mm footprint. Wheels, body and mass are unchanged. This is the layout the Integrator's kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller was tuned for. Expected result is about 69.46, with no new best. This keeps the score floor secure while the remaining iterations test one open geometric question. Slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.145 to 0.147, below the 0.15 trigger, so I am not moving the row forward.
